sentences.text: Under the current UCB Responsible Business Conduct Directions, penal charges for default must be reasonable and levied in a non-discriminatory manner under a Board-approved policy, and they are not meant to be used as a revenue enhancement tool.
Those current directions do not state that a higher default charge may be levied on a retail individual borrower for a non-business loan than on a corporate customer for the same breach.

The earlier 2023 penal-charges circular did say that for loans sanctioned to individual borrowers for purposes other than business, the penal charges must not be higher than those for non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance, but that circular was superseded and is no longer in force.

So, on the current materials, I cannot confirm a rule that authorizes a higher charge for the retail non-business borrower case, and the specific corporate-comparison rule is found only in the superseded circular.
